nodes.name: Execute Workflow Trigger
nodes.notes: FR1: channel-agnostic contract, { chat_id, text } in, { reply_text } out (from 'Return result'). Nothing in this workflow knows it's Telegram -- telegram-adapter.json owns everything channel-specific.

nodes.name: Read settings
nodes.notes: FR16: settings.timezone drives every 'today' calculation below. alwaysOutputData=true (same pattern as retention-sweep.json's 'Read retention_days') so a not-yet-configured account (zero settings rows) still produces one pass-through item -- 'Detect slash command' falls back to the column's own default ('Asia/Colombo') rather than the workflow silently stopping.

nodes.name: Detect slash command
nodes.notes: Reads chat_id/text from the trigger by node-name reference (this node sits two steps downstream of it) and timezone from $json (Read settings' pass-through). Every downstream node in this workflow reads chat_id/text/timezone from THIS node by name, not from the trigger directly.

nodes.name: /today?
nodes.notes: True (index 0) -> Read tasks due today. False (index 1) -> next command check.

nodes.name: Read tasks due today

parameters.query: SELECT id, task_text, deadline FROM tasks WHERE status IN ('todo','in-progress') AND deadline = (now() AT TIME ZONE $1)::date ORDER BY deadline ASC;

nodes.notes: FR5 /today, part 1. 'today' computed in settings.timezone (FR16), not server-local time. alwaysOutputData=true so a zero-row result still lets 'Read open commitments' run next (see that node's notes).

nodes.name: Read open commitments

parameters.query: SELECT id, text, direction, due_date FROM commitments WHERE status = 'open' ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 10;

nodes.notes: FR5 /today, part 2 ('open commitments', either direction -- no direction filter). executeOnce=true because this parameterless query would otherwise re-run once per row 'Read tasks due today' produced (same reason draft-generation.json's 'Read style sample' sets it). alwaysOutputData=true: zero open commitments is a normal, valid result.

nodes.name: /urgent?
nodes.notes: Reached on '/today?' false. True (index 0) -> Read urgent unhandled emails. False (index 1) -> next command check.

nodes.name: Read urgent unhandled emails

parameters.query: SELECT id, subject FROM emails WHERE priority = 'urgent' AND status = 'open' ORDER BY received_at DESC LIMIT 10;

nodes.notes: FR5 /urgent. Explicit columns only (id, subject) -- never SELECT *, consistent with NFR6 even though this path never reaches an LLM.

nodes.name: /deadlines?
nodes.notes: Reached on '/urgent?' false. True (index 0) -> Read open tasks with deadline. False (index 1) -> next command check.

nodes.name: Read open tasks with deadline

parameters.query: SELECT id, task_text, deadline FROM tasks WHERE status IN ('todo','in-progress') AND deadline IS NOT NULL ORDER BY deadline ASC LIMIT 10;

nodes.notes: FR5 /deadlines: soonest-first across every open task with a stated deadline, not just today's.

nodes.name: /vip?
nodes.notes: Reached on '/deadlines?' false. True (index 0) -> Read VIP unhandled emails. False (index 1) -> next command check.

nodes.name: Read VIP unhandled emails

parameters.query: SELECT e.id, e.subject FROM emails e JOIN contacts c ON e.participants @> jsonb_build_array(jsonb_build_object('address', c.email)) WHERE c.is_vip = true AND e.status = 'open' ORDER BY e.received_at DESC LIMIT 10;

nodes.notes: FR5 /vip. Same participants @> jsonb_build_array(jsonb_build_object('address', ...)) join convention as 0006_threads_and_contacts.sql's contact_aggregates view -- the 'address' key is what email-normaliser.json's Normalize node actually writes into emails.participants, not 'email'.

nodes.name: /help?
nodes.notes: Reached on '/vip?' false. True (index 0) -> Format /help reply. False (index 1) -> /week? (added later, ahead of /add? and the free-text path).

nodes.name: Format /help reply

parameters.jsCode: const chatId = $json.chat_id; const reply = 'Just talk to me - plain English works, the slash commands are shortcuts.\n\n' + '/today - tasks due today + open commitments ("what\'s on today?")\n' + '/urgent - unhandled urgent emails ("anything urgent?")\n' + '/deadlines - open tasks with a deadline, soonest first ("what\'s due?")\n' + '/vip - unhandled emails from VIP contacts\n' + '/week - completed/missed this week + next deadline ("how was my week?")\n' + '/add <text> [today|tomorrow] - add a task ("remind me to call the bank tomorrow")\n' + '/done <text> - mark a task done ("mark the report done", "I finished the report")\n' + '/snooze <text> to today|tomorrow - push a task\'s due date ("snooze the report to tomorrow")\n' + '/help - this message\n\n' + 'Anything else I answer from your mail, tasks and commitments, remembering the last few turns (limited per day).'; return { json: { chat_id: chatId, reply_text: reply } };

nodes.notes: FR5 /help. No DB read needed -- $json here is still 'Detect slash command's output, passed straight through by the IF node.

nodes.name: Cap reached?
nodes.notes: True (index 0) -> Budget exhausted reply, no LLM Gateway call (FR8/AC5). False (index 1) -> shortlist candidates and call LLM Gateway.

nodes.name: Budget exhausted reply
nodes.notes: FR8's fixed budget-exhausted reply. No LLM Gateway execution appears in the log for this path (AC5).

nodes.name: Shortlist emails

parameters.query: SELECT id, subject, left(body, 500) AS body, received_at FROM emails WHERE search_vector @@ plainto_tsquery('english', $1) ORDER BY ts_rank(search_vector, plainto_tsquery('english', $1)) DESC LIMIT 5;

nodes.notes: FR6: shortlists via emails.search_vector (0011_search.sql) using the operator's own free-text question as the tsquery input. Explicit columns, truncated body (NFR6) -- never SELECT *, never raw_payload. alwaysOutputData=true so zero matches (a real, expected outcome per spec.md Edge Cases) still lets the shortlist chain continue to tasks/commitments.

nodes.name: Shortlist tasks

parameters.query: SELECT id, task_text, deadline, status FROM tasks WHERE status IN ('todo','in-progress') ORDER BY deadline ASC NULLS LAST, created_at DESC LIMIT 20;

nodes.notes: FR6: recent open tasks as free-text candidates, chained after 'Shortlist emails' (same executeOnce=true convention as draft-generation.json's 'Read style sample', since this parameterless query would otherwise re-run once per upstream row).

nodes.name: Shortlist commitments

parameters.query: SELECT id, text, direction, due_date, status FROM commitments WHERE status = 'open' ORDER BY due_date ASC NULLS LAST, created_at DESC LIMIT 20;

nodes.notes: FR6: recent open commitments as free-text candidates. Same executeOnce=true reasoning as 'Shortlist tasks'.

nodes.name: Build free-text prompt
nodes.notes: FR6/FR7/NFR6. Runs even when all three shortlists are empty (spec.md Edge Cases) -- the LLM Gateway call still happens and still counts against FR8's cap, so the model can say 'I don't see anything matching that' rather than the adapter guessing at a canned response.

nodes.name: Call LLM Gateway
nodes.notes: FR9: LLM Gateway called completely unmodified -- same placeholder-by-cachedResultName convention every other caller (Triage Pipeline, Action Extraction, Draft Generation) uses. workflowId.value left blank; re-point at the real workflow via the resource picker once llm-gateway.json is imported. Its existing Gemini->OpenRouter fallback on quota exhaustion (learnings.md L27/L29) covers the case where the account-wide 20/day quota, not just this workflow's own FR8 cap, is already spent.

nodes.name: Validate free-text result
nodes.notes: FR10: success:false, a timeout (surfaces as success:false from LLM Gateway's own contract), or a missing/empty/non-string answer are all treated as a failure -- routes to the fixed fallback reply, never silence.

nodes.name: Free-text success?
nodes.notes: True (index 0) -> Increment counter and reply. False (index 1) -> Free-text fallback reply (FR10).

nodes.name: Free-text fallback reply
nodes.notes: FR10's fixed fallback reply (AC9) -- no counter increment (see 'Increment counter and reply' notes).

nodes.name: Return result
nodes.notes: Single unified terminal node for all eight possible reply paths (5 slash commands, budget-exhausted, free-text success, free-text fallback) -- same reasoning as llm-gateway.json's own 'Return result': without one convergence point, n8n's sub-workflow completion detection has raced on asymmetric terminal branches in this project before (confirmed live, see llm-gateway.json's notes). telegram-adapter.json (T4) reads this sub-workflow's output as { reply_text } and forwards it to Telegram Send.

parameters.content:
## Assistant Brain

Channel-agnostic: { chat_id, text } in, { reply_text } out. Seven slash commands (/today, /urgent, /deadlines, /vip, /week, /help, /add) each run one fixed parameterized query (or, for /add, one dashboard API call) -- zero LLM cost. Anything else is a free-text question: an independent daily cap (workflow static data, FR8), then a search_vector + tasks + commitments shortlist, a delimited prompt (FR7, same convention as 006-draft-generation), and exactly one LLM Gateway call (FR9, unmodified). Every branch converges on 'Return result' before the trigger returns (FR10, L29's convergence lesson).

/week added later (Phase 7, PHASE-7-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md Wave 5) -- read-only, mirrors GET /api/hub/weekly-review's completed/missed/next-deadline numbers without calling the dashboard.

See .specclaw/changes/012-assistant-bot/spec.md (FR1, FR5-FR10) and design.md (Architecture, Key Decisions).

### Placeholders to fill in on import

- **Supabase Postgres** credential (name 'Supabase Postgres', placeholder id REPLACE_WITH_SUPABASE_POSTGRES_CREDENTIAL_ID) on every Postgres node -- reuse the same credential every prior phase's read nodes already hold, do not create a new one.
- 'Call LLM Gateway' targets the 'LLM Gateway' sub-workflow by name only (workflowId.value blank) -- re-point it at the real workflow via the resource picker once llm-gateway.json is imported.
- Migration 0014_bot_notifications.sql is NOT required for this workflow (it writes nothing) -- only assistant-scheduler.json depends on it.
- FR8's cap (10/day) and the 5-row shortlist limits are starting guesses (design.md Notes) -- revisit once real usage exists.
- No pinData is included here by design (NFR4 fixture-testability instead) -- pin mock data directly on 'Call LLM Gateway's output in the n8n editor when testing AC3/AC4/AC5/AC9.

nodes.name: Read today's usage

parameters.query: SELECT COALESCE((SELECT count FROM bot_free_text_usage WHERE usage_date = $1), 0) AS count;

nodes.notes: 0018_bot_observability.sql, option B2. COALESCE guarantees exactly one row back regardless of whether today has a bot_free_text_usage row yet, so 'Check free-text cap' downstream never has to handle a zero-item case. NOT LIVE-VERIFIED -- see docs/setup/bot-observability-setup.md.

nodes.name: Upsert free-text usage

parameters.query:
INSERT INTO bot_free_text_usage (usage_date, count) VALUES ($1, 1)
ON CONFLICT (usage_date) DO UPDATE SET count = bot_free_text_usage.count + 1;

nodes.notes: 0018_bot_observability.sql, option B2: counted on SUCCESS only (unchanged FR8 reasoning), now persisted instead of workflow static data so it survives an n8n cold start and GET /api/hub/bot-stats can read remaining budget. onError=continueRegularOutput (L28 pattern): a failed usage-count write must not swallow the answer the user is actually waiting for. NOT LIVE-VERIFIED -- see docs/setup/bot-observability-setup.md.

nodes.name: /add?
nodes.notes: Reached on '/week?' false, ahead of the free-text path -- so /add is checked before anything falls through to the LLM. True (index 0) -> Parse /add. False (index 1) -> Compute free-text usage date, same target /help?'s false used to point at directly before /week? was inserted ahead of this node.

nodes.name: Parse /add
nodes.notes: Reads the full command text from Detect slash command ($json.text, passed through unchanged by the If node) -- POST /api/action-items validates a non-empty text itself, so an empty result here (bare '/add' or '/add today') is left to fail there and surface through Format /add reply's error path rather than being special-cased twice.

nodes.name: Login (add)
nodes.notes: Same DASHBOARD_BASE_URL/DASHBOARD_LOGIN_SECRET env vars retention-sweep.json's 'Login' already uses -- no new secret, no new auth mechanism. Named '(add)' only because n8n requires unique node names within a workflow.

nodes.name: Call action-items API
nodes.notes: onError: continueRegularOutput (same as telegram-send.json's 'Call sendMessage') so a validation failure -- empty text, expired cookie -- becomes response data for Format /add reply to read, not a halted workflow. POST /api/action-items already defaults type='task', weight=3, effort_minutes=30 and pushes the created task to Google Calendar when it has a due date -- nothing extra to pass for v1.

nodes.name: /week?
nodes.notes: Phase 7 Wave 5 -- reached on '/help?' false. True (index 0) -> Read week stats. False (index 1) -> /add?, same target '/help?'s false pointed at directly before this node was inserted.

nodes.name: Read week stats

parameters.query:
SELECT
  (SELECT count(*) FROM tasks WHERE status = 'done' AND completed_at > now() - interval '7 days') AS completed_count,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM tasks WHERE status IN ('todo','in-progress') AND deadline IS NOT NULL AND deadline < (now() AT TIME ZONE $1)::date) AS missed_count,
  (SELECT task_text FROM tasks WHERE status IN ('todo','in-progress') AND deadline IS NOT NULL ORDER BY deadline ASC LIMIT 1) AS next_task_text,
  (SELECT deadline FROM tasks WHERE status IN ('todo','in-progress') AND deadline IS NOT NULL ORDER BY deadline ASC LIMIT 1) AS next_deadline;

nodes.notes: Phase 7 Wave 5 -- mirrors GET /api/hub/weekly-review's completed-this-week / missed / next-deadline numbers, read-only, zero LLM cost, same fixed-parameterized-query convention as /today's 'Read tasks due today'. All three scalar subqueries share one FROM-less SELECT so this always returns exactly one row (no executeOnce needed on the next node, same reasoning 'Read today's usage' relies on implicitly). Uses $('Detect slash command') for timezone rather than $json -- this node has no upstream postgres read to inherit pass-through from, but named-reference is the documented convention for every node past the first hop off an IF branch.

nodes.name: Read recent turns

parameters.query: SELECT role, text FROM bot_messages WHERE chat_id = $1 ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 6;

nodes.notes: 0022_bot_messages.sql: the last 6 free-text turns for this chat, newest first ('Build free-text prompt' re-reverses them). This is what makes a follow-up like "and the second one?" answerable. alwaysOutputData + onError=continueRegularOutput (L28 pattern): no history is the normal state on a first message, and a failed read must not swallow the answer.

nodes.name: Log turns

parameters.query: INSERT INTO bot_messages (chat_id, role, text) VALUES ($1, 'user', $2), ($1, 'assistant', $3);

nodes.notes: 0022_bot_messages.sql: written on SUCCESS only, same rule as the usage counter next to it -- a failed answer is not a turn worth remembering. Only the free-text path is logged; the deterministic command branches need no history to answer. onError=continueRegularOutput: a failed write must not swallow the reply.

nodes.name: Match task (done)

parameters.query: SELECT id, task_text FROM tasks WHERE status IN ('todo','in-progress') AND task_text ILIKE ALL($1::text[]) ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 5;

nodes.notes: Order-independent word match (every significant word from 'Parse /done' must appear somewhere in task_text) -- not full-text search (tasks has no search_vector, unlike emails/0011_search.sql), just ILIKE ALL. alwaysOutputData=true (same L-pattern as 'Read tasks due today') so a zero-row result still lets 'Resolve /done match' run and reply, instead of silently dropping the message. NOT LIVE-VERIFIED -- first use of an array-typed positional param in this codebase's n8n queries (see docs/setup); the pg driver binds a JS array to $1::text[] directly, but confirm on first real run.

nodes.name: Login (done)
nodes.notes: Same DASHBOARD_BASE_URL/DASHBOARD_LOGIN_SECRET env vars as Login (add)/retention-sweep.json -- no new secret. Named for uniqueness only, same reason as Login (add).

nodes.name: Match task (snooze)

parameters.query: SELECT id, task_text FROM tasks WHERE status IN ('todo','in-progress') AND task_text ILIKE ALL($1::text[]) ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 5;

nodes.notes: Same order-independent word match as 'Match task (done)' -- see its notes (incl. the NOT LIVE-VERIFIED array-param flag). alwaysOutputData=true so a zero-row result still reaches 'Resolve /snooze match'.

nodes.name: Login (snooze)
nodes.notes: Same DASHBOARD_BASE_URL/DASHBOARD_LOGIN_SECRET env vars as Login (add)/retention-sweep.json -- no new secret. Named for uniqueness only, same reason as Login (add).
